## Description

Programme: MDV-P1-E12 · UX programme: safe, cohesive clinic workspace (from the Nov 2026 product UX audit). Track D (design rules and UI component setup), wave D2. No audit backlog id. Created from the audit's rulings and blueprint, not from a backlog line (see Findings).

Persona and route: /consult/:id · doctor · 1280 px and wider as a rail; 1024 to 1279 as a button in the strip.
Findings and reviewers: F-07, F-04 (to finish) · reviewers A-08 · arbitration ruling 3. Named as a separate ticket by audit backlog UX-14; no UX number of its own.
Rationale: The doctor cannot see who is next, or that a nurse escalated someone, without leaving the note. The first concept showed other patients' names and reasons beside the open note, in view of the patient in the room: the arbitration rejected that.
Proposed UX behaviour: At 1280 px and wider a 200 px rail beside the note lists the doctor's queue in the clinic's queue order: token and age band only, escalations first with the word Escalated (no reason text), then To finish (notes to sign, prescriptions to authorise) as counts. Never a name, a reason or a diagnosis. From 1024 to 1279 px the rail is one button in the strip: Next A-07 · 3 waiting. Choosing another patient keeps today's You have another consultation open challenge. The rail is styled unlike the section anchors, so moving to another chart is a deliberate, distinct act. It can be hidden by the doctor.
Prototype and blueprint reference: docs/product-ux-audit/concepts/medvya-workspace-concept.html, doctor view, audit note 3 (as changed after the debate); docs/product-ux-audit/concepts/screenshots/doctor-1440.png and doctor-1024.png.
Components and tokens affected: SplitLayout region; Chip. No new component.
Front end and back end split: Front end only; reads the ordered queue that the queue-rule ticket exposes.
Prerequisites and blocked by: Blocked by the consultation layout ticket and the queue-rule ticket.
Clinical sign-off: Ask the pilot doctor in the session (doctor scenario step 9) whether the rail helps; not a merge gate.
Effort and regression risk: M · Medium: a list of other patients beside an open note is a wrong-patient risk if it ever shows names; the test below guards that.
Deliberately NOT in this ticket: (1) Names, reasons or complaints in the rail. (2) Switching patient without the open-consultation challenge.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** Given a queue of five patients, when the rail renders, then each row shows a token and an age band and the page holds no other patient's name, complaint or escalation reason
- [ ] **AC2.** Given the rail's test, when a name is added to a row, then the test fails (mutation check)
- [ ] **AC3.** Given an escalated visit, when the rail renders, then it is the first row and carries the word Escalated
- [ ] **AC4.** Given the clinic's queue rule, when the rail and My day are compared, then the order is the same
- [ ] **AC5.** Given an open consultation, when another token is chosen, then the another consultation is open challenge appears and nothing changes until the doctor answers
- [ ] **AC6.** Given 1024 px, when the strip renders, then the rail is the button Next with the token and the waiting count; and axe finds no violation in English or Arabic

## Test notes

- New steps in tests/e2e/consult-studio.spec.ts: rail content, the challenge, the tablet button.
- Real stack: after the handoff walkthrough, the escalated visit is row 1 of the rail.

## Notes / open questions

- Regression risk: medium.
- May be dropped after the pilot doctor's session without loss to any other ticket.
